filename: Improving Oil Slick Trajectory Simulations with Bayesian Optimization.pdf
title: Improving Oil Slick Trajectory Simulations with Bayesian Optimization
parameterization_target: horizontal diffusivity and wind drift factor
code_availability: BayesOpt library at https://github.com/bayesian-optimization/BayesianOptimization; MEDSLIK-II model v2.01 at https://www.medslik-ii.org/index.html; THREDDS catalog at http://thredds.imagine.disi.unitn.it/thredds/catalog/catalog.html
testbed_rationale: The study applies Gaussian-process-based Bayesian optimization for black-box parameter calibration of an existing Lagrangian trajectory model (MEDSLIK-II) rather than generating or validating an ML emulator or ML-based subgrid parameterization dataset.
pain_points: High computational runtime during optimization iterations prevents rapid operational spill response in multi-step calibration mode.
Lack of oil thickness/mass balance information in satellite observations limits calibration to 2D footprint and centroid geometry.
Sensor heterogeneity across satellite passes (SAR vs. optical, Sentinel-1 vs Sentinel-3 vs Landsat 8) introduces observational discrepancies.
Coarse oceanographic forcing in coastal zones lacks local current resolution, forcing reliance on numerical extrapolation.
extraction_notes: The paper uses Bayesian optimization with an Upper Confidence Bound (UCB) acquisition function to calibrate two physical parameters (horizontal diffusivity Kh and wind drift factor alpha) in MEDSLIK-II to maximize the Fractions Skill Score (FSS) against satellite-derived oil spill polygons.
